checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Create draft event group as the seed for an RFQ-only event
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200; EventGroup created with status draft and precomputed_data.creator_fields.creator_quantity populated so EventGroupLineItem#quantity returns 10.0 and #unit_symbol returns 'Nos'.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with status draft and one line item quantity 10 Nos.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and capture the returned event group uuid.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items and assert exactly one active/draft line item is returned.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser with create rights; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} are active in the caller's workspace.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A fresh single-stage draft activates
checkResults.expectedResult: 200; the event group is active with one live stage. Status active; the stage appears in `stages`; a vendor can bid on it.
steps: 1. `PATCH` with `status: "active"` and the stage uuid in `draft_trade_request_uuids`.
checkResults.preconditions: A draft event group with one draft stage that has a bidding-time schedule.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation must never answer with an untyped 500
checkResults.expectedResult: Either 200, or a `render_error_json` failure with a `{code, message}`. Fail if the body is `{"status":500,"error":…}` with no code. Attach the payload to the failure — the payload is what makes the report actionable. The three ranked causes are a `lock_transaction` double-render at `event_groups_controller.rb:74`, `set_customized_audiences` (`trade_controller_helper.rb:687-729`), and `TradeSchedule.change_auction_time(nil)` in `publish_auction`; the third cannot explain the draft-status 500, so an exception class from Sentry is what distinguishes them.
steps: 2. Capture the full response body and the request payload.
checkResults.preconditions: Any valid draft event group and stage.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation of a stage with no bidding-time schedule fails cleanly
checkResults.expectedResult: A `{code, message}` refusal about the schedule. Not a bare 500. This is the regression guard's narrowest form.
checkResults.preconditions: A draft stage whose bidding-time `TradeSchedule` is absent.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation succeeds identically for auction, rfq and rfp stages
checkResults.expectedResult: All three activate. Three active events; report per-mode outcomes separately so a single failure is attributable.
steps: 1. Build three single-stage drafts, one per mode.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation succeeds with one line item and with several
checkResults.expectedResult: Both succeed. Both active with the expected item counts.
steps: 1. Activate a 1-item event and a 2-item event.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation succeeds with a single invited vendor
checkResults.expectedResult: Active with that vendor invited. One audience row for the stage; the vendor can see the event.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation succeeds with a large audience below the cap
checkResults.expectedResult: Active with all of them invited. Audience count equals the request; record the duration.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] More than 500 new audience companies is refused
checkResults.expectedResult: 422, code 511. The event is not activated with 501; the message names the limit.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation succeeds with the pricing sheet filled and with it empty
checkResults.expectedResult: Both succeed at the API layer, or the refusal is a readable one. Record both outcomes; a 500 on either is the finding.
steps: 1. Activate with sheet values present, then with none.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activating a non-existent event group is refused
checkResults.expectedResult: 422, code 533 "Project does not exist." That code and message.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activating a superseded version is refused
checkResults.expectedResult: 422, code 101. The newer version is untouched.
checkResults.preconditions: An event group with a newer version.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] An attachment URL from another company is refused
checkResults.expectedResult: 422, code 101. Nothing written; the event stays draft.
steps: 1. `PATCH` with an attachment URL owned by another company.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A caller without update permission is refused
checkResults.expectedResult: Refused. Event unchanged.
checkResults.preconditions: A user in neither branch.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A Procol-employee CSM can update without the trade permission flag
checkResults.expectedResult: Allowed. The update applies. Then repeat as a Procol employee who is *not* CSM for that company — that must be refused.
checkResults.preconditions: A Procol employee who is CSM for the company, without `trade: create_record`.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Publishing RFP + RFQ where the RFP ends later is refused
checkResults.expectedResult: 422, code 712. Neither stage goes live.
checkResults.preconditions: A two-stage draft with the RFP ending after the RFQ.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A `purchase_request_id` must resolve to an active BOQ PR in the workspace
checkResults.expectedResult: Refused both times (101). No link created.
steps: 1. `PATCH` with an inactive PR id, then with another workspace's PR id.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A draft-status PATCH with line items takes the generic branch
checkResults.expectedResult: Line items are updated; the event stays draft. Status draft; line items reflect the payload.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Line items sent with `status: "active"` are ignored
checkResults.expectedResult: Activation succeeds; the new line item is **not** created. Line-item count unchanged. Record it as expected behaviour, not a bug — but flag it if the UI ever relies on it.
steps: 1. `PATCH` to activate with a new line item in `line_items`.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] `status: "active"` on an already-active event with no draft stages runs no service
checkResults.expectedResult: A coherent response — not a 500, not a silent state change. Assert no state change **and** no 500. ≈ BE-9.6.
checkResults.preconditions: An active event group, no `draft_trade_request_ids`, no `line_items`, no `config`.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Re-activating an already-active event is idempotent
checkResults.expectedResult: No duplicates. Stage count, audience count and bid count identical after the second call.
steps: 1. `PATCH` to activate twice with identical bodies.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Transient config keys are stripped from the persisted config
checkResults.expectedResult: None of them are persisted. All four absent from the stored config.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A terms attachment missing its `type` key is refused cleanly
checkResults.expectedResult: A 4xx with a readable message. Not a 500. ≈ BE-2.22.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Absent `terms_and_conditions.clauses` does not crash activation
checkResults.expectedResult: Activation succeeds both ways. No 500; the stored terms are empty rather than null-broken. ≈ BE-2.24.
steps: 1. `PATCH` with clauses nil, then with the whole key absent.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] A stage absent from `draft_trade_request_uuids` is voided
checkResults.expectedResult: Two live stages; the third voided. The third stage's status is `void`; it is absent from the read payload. ≈ BE-9.3.
checkResults.preconditions: A draft event group with three draft stages.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Adding a draft stage to an already-live event publishes just that stage
checkResults.expectedResult: The new stage goes live; the existing one is untouched, bids intact. Stage count +1; the original stage's bid count unchanged. ≈ BE-2.19.
steps: 1. `PATCH` with `status: "active"` and only the new stage's uuid.
checkResults.preconditions: A live event plus a new draft stage on the same event group.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activating an event group with zero stages is a safe no-op
checkResults.expectedResult: A coherent response, no exception. No 500; the resulting state is explainable. ≈ BE-9.5.
checkResults.preconditions: A draft event group with no stages.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] An approval-gated stage becomes `requested`, not `active`
checkResults.expectedResult: Stage status `requested`; an approval record exists. Status requested; approval present. ≈ BE-9.7.
checkResults.preconditions: gate: publish approval configured.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Auto-routing to the auction team forces the stage to `draft`
checkResults.expectedResult: Stage status draft, assigned to the auction team. Status draft plus the assignment. ≈ BE-9.8.
checkResults.preconditions: gate: `routeAuctionsToAuctionTeam`. An auction stage.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] Activation fires invitation mails exactly once
checkResults.expectedResult: One invitation per vendor overall. Count the enqueued mail jobs across both calls.
steps: 1. Activate, then re-issue the same activation.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.

checkResults.scenario: [RFQ only] The activation response carries the full published shape
checkResults.expectedResult: `stages`, `stage_vs_participants_data`, `config` (including `should_allow_awarding`) and `is_bid_placed_globally` all present. Each key present and internally consistent with the request.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer on the company under test.
